problem: Project state, lifecycle and document authority lived in conversation history and in filenames. A new session could not determine where the work stood, what was next or which document was current, and two audits found the rehabilitation roadmap silently truncated.
scope: Knowledge and process governance only: the project control plane (docs/project), the generic protocol (docs/standards/PROJECT-OPERATING-SYSTEM.md), the RCP validator and its tests, the RCP adoption decision, and the session protocol block in AGENTS.md, plus CF-043/CF-044 recorded in their canonical owner (REC-CONSOLIDATION §1.4). No application business or runtime architecture is touched.
layer: Control policy and repository knowledge governance
baseline: b46c0438d4927851fcd688a8a8e71468aba6cf18; target platform/apps/geostat/backend/api unchanged at 26 modified / 29 untracked; pre-existing dirty backend, ops and docs work preserved and not absorbed into this card.
reuse: Existing owners were inspected and kept: the AIR register owns improvement debt, docs/platform-decisions.md and docs/decisions own ADRs, the recovery registers own findings, requirements, authority and coverage, and governance cards own bounded change records. No second register, roadmap, authority registry or knowledge base was created; pre-existing documents were classified in place, never relocated.
impact: Every session now starts at docs/project/CURRENT.md and ends by running the RCP validator. Adding a governed document requires metadata and a catalogue entry. Twenty-one currency-asserting filenames now carry an assigned authority, and a new one without authority fails RCP-701.
compatibility: No runtime contract, schema, migration, API surface or deployment artifact is affected. The validator is stdlib-only Python and reads repository text; it changes no state. Historical documents keep their content, so all inbound references and evidence remain valid.
failure: The validator fails closed: any unresolved reference, missing authority, vocabulary violation, roadmap gap or duplicate canonical owner exits non-zero and blocks the session-end claim. Rollback is removal of docs/project, docs/standards, the validator and the AGENTS.md control block; no data or runtime state is involved.
security: No credentials, database access, network access or deployment. The validator reads files under the repository root and executes nothing it reads. Digests detect drift but do not authenticate authors.

GOV-001.reason: Existing owners were inspected before anything was created: the AIR register, ADR plane, canonical tree and recovery registers keep their responsibilities; the control plane routes to them and restates none of them.

GOV-002.reason: Every governed artifact carries an explicit authority, in its own header or in the adoption register. RCP-404 fails the build on two canonical owners for one responsibility.

GOV-003.reason: ADR-013 records the decision with alternatives and consequences; identifiers are not reused and the next free identifier is recorded in ADOPTION.

GOV-004.reason: Lifecycle, gates, standing obligations and deferred-hardening triggers are all held by MANIFEST, the single roadmap; RCP-511/512 prevent silent truncation.

ARC-001.reason: One responsibility, one canonical owner is the protocol invariant and is machine checked; the control plane holds no architecture or findings.

ARC-002.reason: Dependency direction is preserved: control artifacts reference knowledge artifacts, never the reverse, and the generic protocol holds zero project facts.

EVO-001.reason: Pre-existing documents are classified, not rewritten or moved; the adoption register carries authority externally so historical evidence stays intact.

OBS-001.reason: The validator reports check count, errors, warnings and governed-artifact count on every run; CURRENT records the last baseline.

SEC-001.reason: No authentication, authorization, tenancy or credential surface is touched. The validator reads repository text only.

SEC-002.reason: No secrets are read, written or logged; the validator executes nothing it finds in the files it validates.

TST-001.reason: 44 negative tests inject one defect per validator check and assert that exact check fires; a check without a test is an incomplete change (OBL-VERIFY-PROVEN).

TST-002.reason: 14 bootstrap tests assert repository-only continuation and 39 coverage tests assert that every mechanism the commissioning specification required still exists, both against the real repository, so decay fails the build instead of going unnoticed.

REL-001.reason: No release surface is touched. The validator is advisory to sessions today; CI wiring is DEF-01 with a firing trigger.

SCH-001.reason: No schema is declared, altered or generated by this change.

SCH-002.reason: No schema versioning or compatibility surface is involved.

SCH-003.reason: No schema-agnostic runtime path is touched.

ING-001.reason: No ingestion mechanism, source contract or import path is involved.

DAT-001.reason: No canonical data, observation or entity storage is read or written.

DAT-002.reason: No data lineage, grain or precision decision is involved.

API-001.reason: No API surface, controller or serving contract is added or changed.

UI-001.reason: No UI or page contract is involved.

handoff: RCP is implemented and machine-enforced; durable knowledge is distributed to canonical owners. Next permitted action is PHASE-002 (Standards & Architecture Quality Benchmark) behind GATE-STANDARDS — not started, and not to be started under this card. Open obligations live in MANIFEST: standing obligations OBL-RCP-VERIFY and OBL-VERIFY-PROVEN, deferred hardening DEF-01..DEF-07, and CLEAN_BUILD_UPGRADE_EQUIVALENCE (UNPROVEN, due before PHASE-010). Two known authority items remain scheduled, not lost: the canonical-directory-blueprint merge (DEF-03) and the object-storage-flow CAD-02 row (DEF-04).
